## How it works

- [statement] The integration user needs API Enabled; Axual specifically requires this permission on the Run As User for its client credentials flow. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/intro-rest-compatible-editions.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations · also: https://docs.axual.io/axual/2026.3/components/run-time/kafka-connect/connect-plugins-catalog/plugins-made-by-axual/salesforce-pubsub-source/index.html
- [statement] For a specific standard or custom object that supports View All Records, CDC requires that permission for the object. Standard objects without it, such as Task and Event, require View All Data. The table lists View All Data for all entities on a channel, plus View All Users when User is included. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-security-perms.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] For single-entity standard CDC channels, Salesforce checks the object permission when subscribing and denies insufficient access. For aggregate and custom channels it enforces permissions on delivery; Pub/Sub API permission changes take effect within 10 minutes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-security-perms.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] Axual documents client credentials and JWT bearer as its two machine-to-machine Pub/Sub authentication flows; client credentials uses a Run As User and JWT requires the integration user to be pre-authorized. This describes that connector, not an exhaustive Salesforce flow list. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-03) — https://docs.axual.io/axual/2026.3/components/run-time/kafka-connect/connect-plugins-catalog/plugins-made-by-axual/salesforce-pubsub-source/index.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] The OAuth client credentials flow does not issue a refresh token or support UI sessions; Salesforce filters out `full`, `web`, and `refresh_token, offline_access` scopes for this flow. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.remoteaccess_oauth_client_credentials_flow_ca.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] Across outstanding FetchRequests or ManagedFetchRequests in one Subscribe or ManagedSubscribe call, the maximum requested-event count is 100; Salesforce treats larger requested counts as 100. This flow-control ceiling is separate from the org’s event-delivery allocation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/allocations.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Exceeding the default delivery allocation disconnects the subscription. Pub/Sub API reports `sfdc.platform.eventbus.grpc.subscription.limit.exceeded` with `You have exceeded the event delivery limit for your org`. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-limits-default.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] Salesforce documents a maximum of 100 outstanding requested events across FetchRequests in a Subscribe call, whereas Axual says Salesforce supports 10,000 events per request in its connector batch-size documentation. Treat these as conflicting source statements; size RPC demand using the primary Salesforce limit and distinguish connector poll batching from wire requests. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/allocations.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations · also: https://docs.axual.io/axual/2026.3/components/run-time/kafka-connect/connect-plugins-catalog/plugins-made-by-axual/salesforce-pubsub-source/index.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Pub/Sub API accepts an OAuth access token or Salesforce session ID; each RPC supplies authentication metadata named `accesstoken`, `instanceurl`, and `tenantid`. WSO2’s connector independently documents supplying the access token, instance URL, and organization ID. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/supported-auth.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations · also: https://mi.docs.wso2.com/en/4.5.0/reference/connectors/sf-pubsub-inbound/sf-pubsub-inbound-endpoint-example/
- [statement] The current Pub/Sub guide lists Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer Editions and excludes Government Cloud; validate Pub/Sub entitlement separately from successful OAuth authentication. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/intro.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] Creating connected apps is restricted as of Spring ’26. Existing connected apps remain usable, while Salesforce recommends external client apps for new integrations; creating further connected apps requires contacting Salesforce Support. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/intro-oauth-and-connected-apps.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] Event deliveries are counted per subscribed client and added across subscribers; a new subscriber consumes additional delivery allocation for the same event. The default pool is shared by high-volume platform events and CDC. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-limits-default.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations · also: https://jamforce.nz/blog/platform-event-limit/, https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/allocations.html
- [statement] For orgs without add-ons, documented default delivery allocations over the last 24 hours are 50,000 for Performance/Unlimited, 25,000 for Enterprise/Professional with API add-on, and 10,000 for Developer. Add-ons move delivery usage to a monthly entitlement model; confirm the actual org entitlement before sizing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-limits-default.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/intro.html
- [statement] The current Pub/Sub allocation page caps unique managed subscriptions at 200 per Salesforce org. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/allocations.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] James Winter reports an incident in which an overnight EmpApi browser subscription consumed the shared delivery allocation while Apex log processing continued. This is a first-person account about an API subscriber, not a measured Pub/Sub outage. (low confidence) — https://jamforce.nz/blog/platform-event-limit/ · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] Salesforce API access requires API access enabled for both the org and user, including the user’s API Enabled permission. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/intro-rest-compatible-editions.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations
- [statement] A platform-event add-on moves event delivery to monthly usage-based entitlement and permits daily spikes through a grace allocation. Salesforce can adjust grace allocations; purchasing an add-on does not promise unlimited delivery. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-limits-entitlement.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/platform-events/guide/platform-events-limits-default.html

## Research summary — Salesforce Pub/Sub OAuth permissions entitlements and allocations

Salesforce Pub/Sub case alerting requires separate checks for authentication metadata, integration-user API access, CDC object permissions, supported org editions, and event delivery capacity. Delivery usage grows across API subscribers and shares a pool with high-volume platform events. Default delivery allocations differ from add-on monthly entitlements. Primary Salesforce limits also need to be distinguished from connector batching settings. A practitioner incident demonstrates how a long-lived browser subscriber can exhaust a shared allocation while internal processing continues.
